commit_message:
avformat/mov: improve HEIF parsing

Parse iprp and iinf boxes and its child boxes to get the actual codec used
(AV1 for avif, HEVC for heic), and properly export extradata and other
properties in a generic way.
The avif tests reference files are updated as the extradata is now exported.

Based on a patch by Swaraj Hota

Co-authored-by: Swaraj Hota <swarajhota353@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: James Almer <jamrial@gmail.com>

fix_commit.message: avformat/mov: don't use an allocated array for sample_size with HEIF images
fix_commit.author: James Almer

findings.title: HEIF still-image stream uses a heap-allocated 1-element sample_sizes array without validating sample_count/chunk_count before it is indexed
findings.message: For HEIF still images, heif_add_stream() synthesizes a MOVStreamContext for the item and allocates sc->sample_sizes (and sc->chunk_offsets/sc->stsc_data/sc->stts_data) as a heap array with exactly one element, unconditionally setting sc->sample_count = 1. Later, in the HEIF item finalization loop (introduced here inline in mov_read_header, later split out as mov_parse_heif_items()), the code writes sc->sample_sizes[0] = item->extent_length and then calls mov_build_index() without first verifying that sc->sample_count and sc->chunk_count are actually still 1. Because MOVStreamContext fields such as sample_count/sample_sizes/chunk_count can be mutated by other generic box parsers that operate on 'the most recently added stream' (e.g. stsz/stsc/stco-style handlers keyed off MOVContext state such as trak_index/last stream index) when a malformed/fuzzed file places such boxes in an unexpected location relative to the synthetic HEIF stream, sc->sample_count or sc->chunk_count can end up inconsistent with the true 1-element array capacity. mov_build_index() then indexes sc->sample_sizes[current_sample] / sc->chunk_offsets[...] for current_sample beyond 0, reading/writing past the 1-element heap allocation, which OSS-Fuzz reported as a NULL pointer dereference (crash inside mov_build_index while processing a HEIF/AVIF stream). Subsequent patches (2aa63784b5 adding an explicit '!=1' check, afbc3a1b23 replacing it with the generic sanity_checks(), 0ffe97d9b9 and 64e6f5d5fa adding narrower fixes) repeatedly tried to patch this design flaw by adding more validation around the array, but the fundamental problem — using a dynamically sized/allocated array to hold what is always exactly one value for a non-animated HEIF image — kept resurfacing as new fuzzer-found NULL/OOB crashes, until it was finally eliminated by replacing the array with the scalar sc->sample_size/sc->stsz_sample_size fields.
findings.suggestion: Do not allocate/use a heap array of size 1 to store the single sample size of a non-animated HEIF/AVIF item. Instead, store the value in the scalar sc->sample_size / sc->stsz_sample_size fields (as done for uniform-size tracks parsed by mov_read_stsz), and keep the existing sanity_checks() call unconditional (without relying on sc->sample_count matching the array capacity), so no code path can index past a 1-element array regardless of what other box parsers may have mutated sc->sample_count/sc->chunk_count to.

ground_truth.root_cause: A single-valued property (the size of the one sample making up a still HEIF/AVIF image) was modeled as a dynamically allocated array sized for the general multi-sample track case, instead of as a scalar. The invariant that this array always has exactly one valid element was not (and, given the surrounding generic box-parsing code, could not reliably be) enforced at every point where the array was later indexed by the shared mov_build_index() logic, leading to out-of-bounds/NULL-like access when the invariant was violated by crafted input.
